answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. The resilience comes from slashing: dishonest approval costs more than the gain from a single manipulated verdict, so rational attackers stay honest. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a lotus as the anchor of the cost.
